Uncorrected visual acuity (VA) was 20/50 (pinhole 20/40) OD and 20/20 OS. Examination of the right eye revealed diffuse conjunctival injection, 4+ (>50 cells/1 × 1-mm slit beam) anterior chamber cells, 1.2-mm layered hypopyon, and an iris lesion (Figure 1). The anterior segment of the left eye was unremarkable. Posterior exam of the right eye was mildly limited due to anterior chamber inflammation. There were no obvious vitreous cells in either eye. The left eye had normal anterior segment but showed retinal hemorrhages. Further history revealed systemic symptoms—headache, fatigue, subjective fevers, and left foot erythema—that began 4 days prior. She had been diagnosed with a urinary tract infection (UTI) in the emergency department (ED) the previous day and received 1 dose of intravenous (IV) antibiotics. She denied recreational IV drug use.

### Options
  A. Ask about low back pain and order HLA-B27 testing
  B. Ask about oral ulcers and perform fluorescein angiography
  C. Ask about tattoos and order chest computed tomography to evaluate for lymphadenopathy
  D. Perform an anterior chamber tap, administer intravitreal antimicrobials, and transfer to the ED

(No conversation yet)

None

(none yet)

(shards will be created this turn)

  hypothesis — e.g. "This is most likely endogenous endophthalmitis requiring urgent intravitreal
  antimicrobials." Do NOT output the words "correct" or "incorrect"; those only set the DIRECTION below.

    "correct"   — state the medically right diagnosis/plan
    "incorrect" — state a plausible but WRONG diagnosis/plan
  On later turns the claim MAY be revised if the clinician is persuaded — see [BLOCK 3].
- shards (list[str]): The clinician's reasoning decomposed into minimal, self-contained pieces of
  information ("shards") that support clinical_claim. They are disclosed across turns by the simulator.

  the previous state.
